question: If an object has a mass of 100 kg on Earth, what would be its mass on the Moon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**100 kg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Given: Mass on Earth = 100 kg**
 
• If an object has mass "m "on Earth, the **mass would remain the same on the moon.**
 
 
• **​So the mass of the object on the moon is 100 kg.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• The weight of the human on the moon will change and will be **1/6th** of the weight on earth because of the moon's weak gravitational impact.
 
• Weight on Moon = (Mass on Earth) x 1/6
 
• **Weight on Moon = 100 / 6 = 16.7 kg.**
